name: rapidfuzz_ratio
description: Normalized Indel similarity scaled to 0–100, the same as Python's `rapidfuzz.fuzz.ratio`. The general-purpose starting point: insertions and deletions lower the score, so near-identical strings score close to 100. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.description: Two strings that differ by one character
examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_ratio('this is a test', 'this is a test!');

columns.name: rapidfuzz_ratio('this is a test', 'this is a test!')

examples.description: Scores below the cutoff are returned as 0
examples.code:
SELECT rapidfuzz_ratio('this is a test', 'this is a test!', score_cutoff := 97) AS below,
       rapidfuzz_ratio('this is a test', 'this is a test!', score_cutoff := 90) AS above;

name: rapidfuzz_partial_ratio
description: The best `rapidfuzz_ratio` of the shorter string against any equally long substring of the longer one. Use it when one string is a fragment of the other, such as a name inside a longer description. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.description: A fragment of a longer string scores 100
examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_partial_ratio('this is a test', 'this is a test!');

columns.name: rapidfuzz_partial_ratio('this is a test', 'this is a test!')

name: rapidfuzz_token_sort_ratio
description: `rapidfuzz_ratio` after splitting both strings on whitespace and sorting the words, so word order is ignored. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_token_sort_ratio('fuzzy wuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

columns.name: rapidfuzz_token_sort_ratio('fuzzy wuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear')

name: rapidfuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio
description: `rapidfuzz_partial_ratio` after sorting the words of both strings: word order is ignored and the shorter string may match part of the longer one. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.description: Reordered words where one string is shorter
examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

columns.name: rapidfuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear')

name: rapidfuzz_token_set_ratio
description: Compares the sets of words in both strings, ignoring word order and repeated words. Scores 100 when the words of one string are a subset of the other's. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.description: Repeated words do not lower the score
examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_token_set_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'fuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

columns.name: rapidfuzz_token_set_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'fuzzy fuzzy was a bear')

name: rapidfuzz_partial_token_set_ratio
description: `rapidfuzz_partial_ratio` applied to the word sets of both strings. Scores 100 as soon as the strings share a word, so it is a loose filter rather than a ranking score. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_partial_token_set_ratio('fuzzy was a bear but not a dog', 'fuzzy was a bear');

columns.name: rapidfuzz_partial_token_set_ratio('fuzzy was a bear but not a dog', 'fuzzy was a bear')

name: rapidfuzz_token_ratio
description: The higher of `rapidfuzz_token_sort_ratio` and `rapidfuzz_token_set_ratio`, computed in one pass, which is faster than calling both. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.description: Best of the sorted-word and word-set comparisons
examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_token_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

columns.name: rapidfuzz_token_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear')

name: rapidfuzz_partial_token_ratio
description: The higher of `rapidfuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio` and `rapidfuzz_partial_token_set_ratio`, computed in one pass. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

name: rapidfuzz_wratio
description: Weighted ratio, the same as Python's `rapidfuzz.fuzz.WRatio`: combines `rapidfuzz_ratio` with the partial and token scorers, weighting them by how different the string lengths are. A good default when you do not know how the strings differ. It is several times slower than `rapidfuzz_ratio`. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.description: Different lengths and an extra word
examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_wratio('this is a test', 'this is a new test!!!');

columns.name: rapidfuzz_wratio('this is a test', 'this is a new test!!!')

name: rapidfuzz_qratio
description: Quick ratio, the same as Python's `rapidfuzz.fuzz.QRatio`: `rapidfuzz_ratio`, except that it returns 0 when either string is empty. Returns a `DOUBLE` from 0 to 100. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Scores below this value (0–100) are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

name: rapidfuzz_levenshtein_distance
description: Levenshtein distance: the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn s1 into s2. Unlike DuckDB's built-in `levenshtein`, it counts Unicode characters rather than bytes, and each kind of edit can be weighted. Returns the distance: 0 means identical. Returns `BIGINT`. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: replace_cost
parameters.description: Cost of substituting a character. A cost of 2 or more makes a substitution no cheaper than a deletion plus an insertion.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Distances above this value are returned as score_cutoff + 1, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.code:
SELECT rapidfuzz_levenshtein_distance('café', 'cafe') AS rapidfuzz,
       levenshtein('café', 'cafe') AS builtin;

name: rapidfuzz_levenshtein_similarity

Unlike DuckDB's built-in `levenshtein`, it counts Unicode characters rather than bytes, and each kind of edit can be weighted. Returns the similarity: higher is more similar. Returns `BIGINT`. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.description: Similarities below this value are returned as 0, which lets RapidFuzz skip work on poor matches. Must be between 0 and 1. NULL means no cutoff.

name: rapidfuzz_extract
description: The best matches for `query` among `choices`, best first, like Python's `rapidfuzz.process.extract`. Returns a list of up to `top_k` structs with the `choice`, its `score` and its 1-based `choice_index` in `choices`; ties keep the order of `choices`. The query is preprocessed once and reused for every choice. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: choices
parameters.description: The candidates. NULL entries are skipped but keep their position.

parameters.name: scorer
parameters.description: The similarity used to rank the choices: any ratio name ('ratio', 'partial_ratio', 'token_sort_ratio', 'partial_token_sort_ratio', 'token_set_ratio', 'partial_token_set_ratio', 'token_ratio', 'partial_token_ratio', 'wratio', 'qratio') or a normalized similarity ('<metric>_normalized_similarity', e.g. 'levenshtein_normalized_similarity', 'jaro_winkler_normalized_similarity'). Case-insensitive.

parameters.name: top_k
parameters.description: The maximum number of matches to return. NULL returns all of them.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Choices scoring below this value are skipped. The range follows the scorer: 0–100 for ratios, 0–1 for normalized similarities. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.description: The two best matches by sorted words
examples.code:
SELECT rapidfuzz_extract('new york jets', ['New York Jets', 'New York Giants', 'Dallas Cowboys'],
                         scorer := 'token_sort_ratio', top_k := 2) AS matches;

rows: [{'choice': New York Jets, 'score': 76.92307692307692, 'choice_index': 1}, {'choice': New York Giants, 'score': 64.28571428571428, 'choice_index': 2}]

examples.code:
SELECT m.choice, round(m.score, 1) AS score, m.choice_index
FROM (SELECT unnest(rapidfuzz_extract('cowboys', ['New York Jets', 'New York Giants', 'Dallas Cowboys'], score_cutoff := 25)) AS m);

name: rapidfuzz_extract_one
description: The single best match for `query` among `choices`, like Python's `rapidfuzz.process.extractOne`: a struct with the `choice`, its `score` and its 1-based `choice_index`, or NULL when no choice reaches `score_cutoff`. Ties go to the earlier choice. Strings are compared by Unicode character, not by UTF-8 byte.

parameters.name: choices
parameters.description: The candidates. NULL entries are skipped but keep their position.

parameters.name: scorer
parameters.description: The similarity used to rank the choices: any ratio name ('ratio', 'partial_ratio', 'token_sort_ratio', 'partial_token_sort_ratio', 'token_set_ratio', 'partial_token_set_ratio', 'token_ratio', 'partial_token_ratio', 'wratio', 'qratio') or a normalized similarity ('<metric>_normalized_similarity', e.g. 'levenshtein_normalized_similarity', 'jaro_winkler_normalized_similarity'). Case-insensitive.

parameters.name: score_cutoff
parameters.description: Choices scoring below this value are skipped. The range follows the scorer: 0–100 for ratios, 0–1 for normalized similarities. NULL means no cutoff.

examples.description: The best match by weighted ratio
examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_extract_one('cowboys', ['New York Jets', 'New York Giants', 'Dallas Cowboys']) AS best;
SELECT rapidfuzz_extract_one('zzz', ['New York Jets', 'New York Giants', 'Dallas Cowboys'], score_cutoff := 50) AS best;

examples.description: Map every input to its closest known value
examples.code:
SELECT name, rapidfuzz_extract_one(name, ['Acme Corporation', 'Globex Industries', 'Initech'],
                                   scorer := 'token_set_ratio').choice AS canonical
FROM customers
ORDER BY id
LIMIT 4;

name: rapidfuzz_levenshtein_editops
description: The Levenshtein edit operations that turn s1 into s2: a list of structs with the `operation` ('insert', 'delete' or 'replace') and the positions `s1_pos` and `s2_pos` it applies at. Positions are 0-based character offsets and ranges are half-open, as in Python's `rapidfuzz`.

examples.code:
SELECT op.operation, op.s1_pos, op.s2_pos
FROM (SELECT unnest(rapidfuzz_levenshtein_editops('kitten', 'sitting')) AS op);

name: rapidfuzz_levenshtein_opcodes
description: Describes how to turn s1 into s2 as blocks that cover both strings: each struct has an `operation` ('equal', 'insert', 'delete' or 'replace') and the ranges `s1_start`–`s1_end` and `s2_start`–`s2_end`. Useful for highlighting differences. Positions are 0-based character offsets and ranges are half-open, as in Python's `rapidfuzz`.

examples.code:
SELECT op.operation, op.s1_start, op.s1_end, op.s2_start, op.s2_end
FROM (SELECT unnest(rapidfuzz_levenshtein_opcodes('kitten', 'sitting')) AS op);

name: rapidfuzz_indel_editops
description: The Indel edit operations ('insert' or 'delete', no substitutions) that turn s1 into s2, as structs with `operation`, `s1_pos` and `s2_pos`. Positions are 0-based character offsets and ranges are half-open, as in Python's `rapidfuzz`.

name: rapidfuzz_indel_opcodes
description: Describes how to turn s1 into s2 as 'equal', 'insert' and 'delete' blocks covering both strings, based on Indel edits. Each struct has `operation`, `s1_start`, `s1_end`, `s2_start` and `s2_end`. Positions are 0-based character offsets and ranges are half-open, as in Python's `rapidfuzz`.

examples.code:
SELECT op.operation, op.s1_start, op.s1_end, op.s2_start, op.s2_end
FROM (SELECT unnest(rapidfuzz_indel_opcodes('kitten', 'sitting')) AS op);

name: rapidfuzz_partial_ratio_alignment
description: The `rapidfuzz_partial_ratio` score together with where it was found: a struct with `score` and the ranges `s1_start`–`s1_end` and `s2_start`–`s2_end` of the best-matching substrings. Positions are 0-based character offsets and ranges are half-open, as in Python's `rapidfuzz`.
